title: Envelope: response (v2)
description: Carries the v1 shape (parent, result, to) plus P6's incompleteness fields: unmet[], blocked_by, attempted, standing, residue. New fields land only on this new file (P4 discipline) rather than widening the shipped v1 response or the shared v2 base (P4 D1).

then.description: D1's third clause: today's refusal (no unmet+blocked_by) would force `XS-seomatrix-20260801-p1pf` — every criterion answered, shortfall is standing, not completeness — to either mark a met criterion unmet or drop to `answered` and lose the caveat. So a `partial`/`cannot` is accepted when it names what is unmet AND what would unblock it, OR when it declares a non-authoritative standing (a bare `standing: authoritative` supplies no new signal and does not satisfy this branch).

to.description: Exchange type (X class, not decision): exactly one target system.

unmet.description: Which of the parent's acceptance_criteria[] this response did not satisfy — never by restating the criterion in prose (AC4), so the record cannot drift from what the parent actually asked. defects-fix-2026-08 P3: HOMOGENEOUS — either every entry is a bare INDEX into that array (an ordinal-only parent) or every entry is {criterion: <id>} (a parent whose acceptance_criteria[] declares ids); a mixed array is refused. May be present and empty: a `standing`-only shortfall (D1's `p1pf`) answered every criterion and has nothing to list here.

blocked_by.description: What would unblock the unmet criteria (US-1). `owner` is checked against fold.CheckLegality per P-2 before any surface reports it (P1's transferred AC4) — that check is a later wave's, not this schema's.

reason_code.description: Mirrors event/v2's reason_code enum (schemas/event/v2/event.schema.json) — the same vocabulary, not a second list. Mirrored rather than $ref'd: internal/schema/corpus.go registers only refTarget entries (the per-version base schema) at their own $id-derived URL, so a cross-family $ref from this file has nothing to resolve against without a corpus.go change this wave does not make.

owner.description: The system actually being waited on — not necessarily the response's own target (P1's US-3 attribution fix).

needs.description: Closed vocabulary (plan Q1), deliberately not free text. `bytes` is the only spec-named member (the live XS-seomatrix-20260801-6vr2 case: a committed review tree or a fetch locator). `judgement` and `decision` widen it per Q1's own priced examples — a native-speaker judgement and an owner decision — neither named verbatim by the spec, so this enumeration is this wave's own call; see the Deviations report.

attempted.description: What WAS done, so "0 of N, reported" is distinguishable from silence (US-2, AC3).

standing.description: Whether the supplier is entitled to make these values binding (D1 — a regression fix, not an addition). A `partial` whose shortfall is standing rather than completeness carries this with an EMPTY unmet[].

criterion_index.description: Index into the parent's acceptance_criteria[] whose non-met verdict is carried forward. Mutually exclusive with `criterion` below (defects-fix-2026-08 P3) — an ordinal-only parent uses this; a parent whose acceptance_criteria[] declares ids uses `criterion` instead.

criterion.description: Names the parent's acceptance_criteria[].id whose non-met verdict is carried forward (defects-fix-2026-08 P3). Mutually exclusive with `criterion_index` above.

carried_to.description: The successor artifact id that inherits the open criterion.

allOf.description: Naming BOTH criterion_index and criterion on one entry is refused — same shape as event/v2's own verdicts[] index/criterion exclusivity, and the same reason: two identities for one binding has no single answer.
Naming NEITHER is refused too — an entry must name what it carries forward.

residue.description: Where a non-met criterion goes when a terminal transition (close/withdraw/cancel) would otherwise extinguish it silently (D3, AC8). Shape only: the refusal — a terminal transition over a parent with a non-met verdict and no residue — depends on the closing event and the parent's verdicts, neither of which a response instance carries; that cross-artifact check belongs to internal/validate, off this wave's allowlist.
